name: tortoise
description: Tortoise ORM 1.1.9 in_transaction() through tortoise.backends.asyncpg and asyncpg 0.32.0. postgres:// selects that engine. A nested in_transaction() is a savepoint. Category C faults are withheld or rewritten in this process, on asyncpg.Connection.execute, before Tortoise sees the error. A transaction ROLLBACK is the statement "ROLLBACK;". The pool reset's "ROLLBACK" has no semicolon and is not withheld. Pool maxsize is 1, the catalog's pool_max. Tortoise's own default maxsize is 5.

modes.description: in_transaction() for the outer transaction and a nested in_transaction() for the savepoint. Engine tortoise.backends.asyncpg, the engine postgres:// selects. minsize 1, maxsize 1. The pool is not closed between TX-03's two units.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: Tortoise 1.1.9 has no propagation mode that promises an independent transaction. A nested in_transaction() is a savepoint: NestedTransactionContext calls savepoint() (tortoise/backends/base/client.py). Model.save sends its INSERT when it is called, so a nested scope has no pending outer writes it could commit.

TX-05.managed-serializable.reason: tortoise.transactions.in_transaction accepts only a connection name (tortoise/transactions.py, 1.1.9). It does not accept an isolation level. asyncpg.Connection.transaction(isolation=...) is the driver, not a Tortoise API.

TX-05.explicit-serializable.reason: Tortoise 1.1.9 has no explicit transaction API that accepts an isolation level. in_transaction() is a context manager, and its signature has no isolation argument.

MG-02.held.reason: Tortoise ORM 1.1.9 exposes no migration runner, history table, or reversal. Aerich is a separate project and is not this adapter.
